- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.28), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 3-day moving average to smooth initial forecast.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% lag correction to forecast for next 5–7 days.
